PullRequest.Title: Chat windows: keep the user's arrangement when parts are hidden or shown and across reloads
PullRequest.Body:

## Bug

In a chat window (session or chat **Open in > New Window**), swap the chat and editor parts by dragging the editor part's grabber to the left of the chat. Then hide the editor and show it again. The editor comes back on the **right**, the default side, instead of where the user put it.

Reproduced on `main` (a96ab7ddc8e) with every entry point: the Session Activity Bar's **Show Editor**, **Configure Layout > Show Editor**, Show Editor off then the **Files** entry, and **Configure Layout > Show Chat** (Editor Only), off and on. Each time the parts went back to chat-left, editor-right.

## Cause

Every hide/show is a layout-mode change (Side by Side ↔ Chat Only / Editor Only). `ChatWindowGrid._update` rebuilt the grid from the new mode's own arrangement whenever the user had moved a part. Chat Only and Editor Only also had arrangements of their own: Editor Only used the stacked one, and Chat Only moved terminals under the editor across the bottom. This was the deliberate contract from #345683, which existing tests locked in. It is not a regression.

## Change

The contract is reversed: hiding or showing the chat or the editor never re-arranges the parts, from any entry point.

- `ChatWindowGrid` arranges the parts for the window's **split layout** (side by side or stacked). Chat Only and Editor Only hide the chat or the editor in place in that arrangement. Only switching between side by side and stacked, or **Reset Chat Window Layout**, arranges the parts anew.
- A hidden part's terminals stay in place. For example, with the terminals under the editor, Chat Only keeps them in their column beside the chat.
- A part shown again gets back the room it had in its row or column, instead of SplitView taking it from the last view (often the terminals).

### Sizes: one record of how the parts show together

- Part sizes are remembered as both parts show, in `sessions.chatWindow.chatSizes.v2`, keyed by the split layout's arrangement. There is no separate record per hidden mode. While a part is hidden, a sash the user drags or resets is saved as the sizes both parts take once the hidden one shows again (its row or column reconciled from the shares before it hid).
- Only the dimension the user changed is saved. Sizes the parts only take to fit, such as beside terminals taller than the window or below a part's least size, are not saved as the user's.
- The terminals' height is one shared preference, saved only when the user changes their height.
- Fixed chrome (the title row, the Session Activity Bar strip) keeps its size and never takes a share.
- Compatibility: older entries keyed with a hidden mode are kept but no longer read; those modes start from the split layout's sizes.

### Arrangements across reloads

- New per-chat workspace record `sessions.chatWindow.chatArrangements` (last 200 chats): `{ version: 1, splitLayout, orientation, width, height, root }`, where `root` is the part grid's serialized tree without the terminals and the parts the grid created, which restore as before.
- It is stored only when the arrangement differs from the default one, with the part sizes on `onWillSaveState`, before the window unloads, and as the window starts closing. It is read once when the grid is created, and used only if its version, split layout and cells match. Anything else, including corrupt or non-finite data, falls back to the default arrangement.
- A restored arrangement keeps its split when the terminals first show in it: added at startup, registered empty and filled later (as the terminals service does), or joining later. This happens once; later shows keep the sizes the user gave the parts.
- **Reset Chat Window Layout** deletes the record.

### Part grid

- `serializeGrid()` serializes the cells without every part's groups, and `getCellMinimumSize()` reports a cell's least size.
- A cell that does not show when it joins the grid (a part without editors, or a hidden cell) is now added invisible at its size. It no longer joins visible and hides at once, which took its room from the cells beside it and gave all of it back to the last one. Where nothing else would show in the row or column it joins, the previous path is kept. The part grid's other users (two screenshot fixtures) only add visible views and are unaffected.

### Review

An independent review on a different model ran 12 rounds over the full change. It covered hidden-part sizes, terminals joining or leaving while a part is hidden, created parts, fixed chrome, windows too small for the terminals, and restored arrangements with and without the chrome. Each finding was fixed with a regression test; the final round approved `dc5a2c72ba8` with no remaining findings.

## How to test

1. Open a session in a new chat window, open **Files**, and drag the editor's grabber to the left of the chat (or drag the chat onto the right edge of the editor).
2. Hide and show the editor with the Session Activity Bar's Show Editor (with `sessions.sessionActivityBar.showLayoutActions`), Configure Layout > Show Editor, the Files entry, and Configure Layout > Show Chat. The editor stays left of the chat, at its size.
3. Add a terminal, hide the editor, drag the sash beside the terminals, and show the editor: it takes that width. Quit and relaunch: the arrangement and sizes come back.
4. Run **Reset Chat Window Layout**. The chat is on the left again, also after another relaunch.
5. Configure Layout > Stacked, then Side by Side. The parts are arranged from the mode.

## Validation

- Red test before the fix: "the main part moved to the left of the chat stays there as the editor hides and shows again" failed; the shape went to `row(chat, main)` after Chat Only. Each later fix was red-checked against its parent commit.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/{chatWindow/test/**/*,test/browser/parts/partGrid/*}.test.js"`: passed, 388 tests (317 chat window, 71 part grid). They include audit tables over the hide/show sequences, gestures (width, height, sash reset) in windows too small for the terminals or for the parts' least sizes, with and without the chrome, and reload; and the terminals' first show in a restored arrangement in each real order.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed. `pnpm run eslint <changed files>`: passed. `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed (later changes add no imports).
- Neighboring suites (sessions chat window, sessions layout, Session Activity Bar): 4 `DesktopLayoutController` "[review] empty Changes retains populated checks…" tests fail identically on `main`; they are pre-existing and unrelated.
- CI: Screenshots and Playwright Fixture Tests pass.
- Live, on a Code - OSS dev build from `main`: the bug reproduced with every entry point listed above.
- Live, on a Code - OSS dev build of `dc5a2c72ba8` (isolated profile, 6 launches): passed.
  - Swap, then hide/show from the strip and Configure Layout (editor and chat), and Chat Only → Editor Only → Side by Side directly: the editor stays left at its width, the terminals at their height.
  - Terminals closed and re-added while the editor is hidden; window resized while hidden (a real window resize through a test-harness-only endpoint, not part of this change); Stacked with the chat moved above the editor and full-width terminals: sizes identical after showing again.
  - Reload after a width drag, a sash reset, or widening the terminals column while the editor is hidden: the arrangement and sizes come back.
  - With the Session Activity Bar hidden by setting: a swapped arrangement and a reordered Stacked one come back after reload. The first terminal of the session shows in them without changing the split or squeezing the editor.
  - Window shorter than the terminals, a width dragged while the editor is hidden, then reload: the width comes back, and so does the terminals' height, not the squeezed one.

## Not covered

- A part created for dropped editors, added or closed while a part is hidden, was verified in unit tests only; it was not driven live.
- Restoring an arrangement into a grid without the title row and strip is covered by unit tests. In the Agents window, both chrome cells always exist (the strip only hides by setting), so that path is not reachable live.
- Reload checks allow one point of difference in a split's share, as sizes round to whole pixels.
- Live checks used CDP focus emulation and keybindings bound to the chat window, not OS focus.

## Known, not in this PR

- A chat window left in Chat Only comes back Side by Side after a relaunch; this PR does not read or write the layout mode.
- After the editor shows in a window shorter than the terminals and the window grows again, the terminals keep their squeezed height until a reload, which restores their saved height.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reload a chat window and restore a user-arranged grid
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The service synchronously reads the existing size record and the new arrangement record before constructing ChatWindowGrid; arrangement validation and the first grid restore/layout must finish before the auxiliary window is laid out.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Each arrangement lookup scans at most 200 stored chats, and each accepted arrangement contains only the chat, main part, and optional two chrome cells; restored grid work scales with the current small cell tree.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous construction path per opened auxiliary chat window; separate window opens are serialized per chat by the existing keyed sequencer, with no new aggregate remote-operation burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PerChatMemory reparses the in-memory storage string on each get and has no parsed-object cache, but records are capped at 200 and invalid/cold entries fall back once to the default arrangement. There is no network/filesystem cache miss on this path because storage get reads the initialized storage cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the constructor call path, 200-entry cap, validation, and synchronous grid restoration are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact stored JSON size and number of concurrently opened chat windows vary, but accepted arrangement trees are structurally restricted to the window cells.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added startup work is bounded to one small cached-storage scan and one small grid restore per opened chat window, without expensive boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hide/show chat or editor parts, change split layout, and let terminals join, move, empty, or refill
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable updates synchronously serialize and compare the small grid, toggle visibility, and sometimes resize or rebuild grid rows before the layout-mode or terminal-state transition completes.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the number of grid cells and created editor parts. Normal grids have chat, main, terminal, and up to two chrome cells; serialization is triggered by user/state transitions rather than every frame of sash movement.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates run synchronously through one autorun and PartGrid event chain per window; no promises, queues, subprocesses, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls are reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pre-hide and pre-first-terminal serialized snapshots are retained in memory and replaced on relevant arrangement changes, then cleared when both parts show, split layout changes, reset occurs, or terminals first show.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: event sources and snapshot lifecycle are directly traceable through the changed methods and PartGrid's arrangement event.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users can create extra editor parts, but realistic cell counts are low; the retained created-ID set could grow only through repeated create-resize-close cycles while a part remains hidden and is released on ordinary mode/layout transitions or disposal.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: synchronous tree work is bounded and gesture/state-driven, and retained snapshots have clear lifecycle exits under realistic use.

Scenarios.Scenario: Periodic storage flush, focus loss, shutdown, reset, or auxiliary-window unload persists sizes and arrangements
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each open chat window's synchronous onWillSaveState/onBeforeUnload handler exports the grid, parses the capped per-chat arrangement list, and stringifies/stores it when custom; this completes before the storage flush or unload proceeds. The backend database flush occurs afterward and is off the synchronous export/serialization portion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the new sessions.chatWindow.chatArrangements workspace-storage value through the storage backend after synchronous collection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one arrangement store per open custom-arranged chat window per save signal; default arrangements call delete, which the changed PerChatMemory.delete avoids storing when absent. Existing size persistence remains one store per window. Storage signals occur on the one-minute idle flush, focus loss, shutdown, and unload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same handler already exported and stored sizes per open window, but did not export or store a separate arrangement record.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous export/parse/stringify is on the save/unload path; the underlying backend flush is awaited by storage flush but changes for the same key are buffered/coalesced by the storage layer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU/allocation scales with open chat-window count times at most 200 small stored arrangements; persisted history is capped and each exported arrangement strips terminals and dynamically created parts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Storage listeners run synchronously and sequentially on the main thread; open windows do not issue concurrent arrangement writes, and the final backend flush handles queued storage updates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PerChatMemory has no parsed cache, but storage itself is initialized/cached; set rewrites the capped list, while delete now negative-checks and skips unchanged absent records.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous per-window serialization and introduced storage operation; medium for physical database-write cardinality because the storage backend buffers same-key updates.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The maximum practical count of simultaneously open chat windows is not explicit, but the per-record tree and retained history are tightly bounded; exact backend write coalescing is implementation-dependent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this adds bounded periodic serialization and one buffered workspace-storage key, but evidence does not establish user-visible latency or excessive I/O under realistic open-window counts.

Scenarios.Scenario: Add an initially invisible part-grid cell, including empty terminal/editor parts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: PartGrid computes the reference/edge extent and inserts the cell with Sizing.Invisible or a serialized visible:false node during the explicit add operation, then performs the existing visibility/look update.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with explicit cell additions and, for edge rebuild cases, the current grid tree size; it is not on scroll, typing, frame, or resize loops.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous grid mutation per added cell; no asynchronous or external boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; visibility is derived from the current cell state and immediately committed to the grid.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed addCell/addAtEdge branches and PartGrid arrangement event are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Other PartGrid consumers may have different small cell shapes, but changed behavior applies only to cells already determined not to show.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the extra model reads and visibility flagging are constant/small-tree work on a cold structural mutation and avoid the prior visible-then-hidden relayout.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all six changed files and paginated diffs. Traced startup restore, hide/show and terminal transitions, save/unload persistence, generic invisible-cell insertion, snapshot ownership, storage bounds, event cadence, and external boundaries. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced.
